title: Symlink Removal Validating the Link Target
pattern: A symlink unlink operation resolves the link and returns an error or throws when the target it points to does not exist (a dangling link).
why_bad: Removing a symlink operates on the link itself, not on its target. Checking the target conflates link removal with target validation, and it makes the operation fail in the most common reason to remove a link: it is dangling.
detection: Symlink deletion code calling `read_link`/`canonicalize`/`metadata` (which follows links) and `target.exists()` before `remove_file` on the link path, returning `Err` when the target is missing.
counterexample: Integrity or migration tools whose explicit purpose is to verify link targets before removing links.
source: John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Section 10.4; Marianne Bellotti, *Kill It with Fire*, Chapter 3.
